info.title: dbt Cloud
info.x-itential-curated: Trimmed to 29 of 207 upstream operations (v2 API 2.0.0 + v3 API 3.0.0 combined), covering Jobs, Runs, Projects, Environments, and Connections CRUD/execution for automation. See the repo README for the full breakdown and the full v2/v3 specs.
info.description: dbt Cloud is the managed service for running dbt (data build tool) transformation jobs, orchestrating analytics engineering pipelines, and managing dbt projects, environments, and warehouse connections.

post.description: Use this endpoint to kick off a run for a job. When this endpoint returns a successful response, a new run will be enqueued for the account. Users can poll the Get run endpoint to poll the run until it completes. After the run has completed, users can use the Get run artifact endpoint to download artifacts generated by the run.

Use this endpoint to retry a failed run for a job from the point of failure, if the run failed. Otherwise trigger a new run. When this endpoint returns a successful response, a new run will be enqueued for the account. Users can poll the Get run endpoint to poll the run until it completes. After the run has completed, users can use the Get run artifact endpoint to download artifacts generated by the run.

get.description: Retrieve the list of artifacts generated for a run.

parameters.name: include_related
parameters.description: Comma-separated list of related objects to include in the response.

get.description:
Use this endpoint to fetch artifacts from a completed run. Once a run has been completed, you can use this endpoint to download the `manifest.json`, `run_results.json`, or `catalog.json` files from dbt platform. These artifacts contain information about the models in your dbt project, timing information around their execution, and a status message indicating the result of the model build. 

For dbt Fusion job runs, you can also use this endpoint to fetch the per-step OpenTelemetry (OTel) telemetry artifact at `metadata/telemetry-<step>-otel.parquet`. You'll receive it as `application/x-parquet`, and it contains node outcomes, test outcomes, and timing for the step. 

By default, you get artifacts from the last step in the run. To fetch artifacts from other run steps, use the `step` query parameter below.

parameters.name: include_related
parameters.description: Comma-separated list of related objects to include in the response.

parameters.name: step
parameters.description: The index of the Step in the Run to query for artifacts. The first step in the run has the index `1`. If the `step` parameter is omitted, then this endpoint will return the artifacts compiled for the last step in the run.

List of cost optimization features to enable for this job.

Valid values:
  • "state_aware_orchestration" - Enable orchestration that adapts to state changes (Private beta, requires fusion)
  • "efficient_testing" - Aggregate generic tests into a single query and reuse redundant tests (Private beta, requires fusion)

  • "inherit_environment" - Inherit this job's dbt State setting from its environment. Must be sent on its own; it cannot be combined with any other value.
Example: ["dbt_state"]

job_completion_trigger_condition.description:
Use this to set up job completion triggers which would trigger a run of a job when another run finishes. If you have a child job that you want triggered on the completion of a parent job, then configure the trigger on the child job to be on job completion and select the project, parent job and the statuses of the parent job on which to trigger the child job. The statuses which is an array can be one or more of:
  • success (10)
  • error (20)
  • canceled (30)
Once the parent job completes, a new run will be enqueued for the child job.
Example of a job completion trigger:
            {
                "condition": {
                    "job_id": 1,
                    "project_id": 1,
                    "statuses": [10, 20],
                }
            }
